### 21. Out-of-office with a leave time and a return time (issue #6)

*Opened 2026-10-07, from the Sprint 1 check after HANDOFF 22.* Issue #6 is Zach's second
medium issue for Sprint 1. Nothing is built. The sprint is due **2026-10-08, 11:59 PM**.

**Model: Deep (Fable 5.1). Lane C. Waits on nothing. Own worktree:
`.claude/worktrees/issue-6`, branch `feat/issue-6-ooo-leave-return-time` off `origin/main`.**
Deep because the core of this item is the slot engine: a timezone or boundary mistake there
compiles, passes every gate, and offers bookings while the host is away. Build it in the session
itself, not in a subagent. If you are not Fable 5.1, stop and say so before you read anything else.

You are picking up cal.diy, the `CSCI-435-SE` course fork of Cal.com. Read, in this order:
`CLAUDE.local.md`; `HANDOFF.md` steps 20 and 22; `docs/AGENT-PRACTICES.md` Part 1, Part 6 and
Part 7; `CONTRIBUTING.md`; `AGENTS.md`; and the `agents/rules/*.md` files for what you touch, at
least `data-repository-pattern.md`, `data-prefer-select-over-include.md`,
`performance-dayjs-usage.md`, `performance-avoid-quadratic.md`, `quality-error-handling.md`,
`testing-timezone.md`. Session rules, inline because this prompt travels alone:
- Run `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH"` before any yarn command.
- **Never `git commit` or `git push`.** Print `git add <exact files>` (with `git add -N` for new
  files) and `git commit -o <same files> -m "feat: ... (#6)"`, lowercase, and stop. Never
  `git add -A` or `git add .`. No `Co-Authored-By` line, no "Generated with" line, anywhere,
  including the PR body.
- `select`, never `include`, in Prisma. No `as any`. No API, option or field you have not seen in
  this checkout. Strings go through `t()` and `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.
- Gates always forced: `yarn type-check:ci --force`, `yarn lint --force`, and
  `TZ=UTC yarn test --exclude '**/.claude/**'`. Without the exclude, other worktrees double the
  test count and fake failures. Also run `VITEST_MODE=timezone yarn test --exclude '**/.claude/**'`,
  because this item is timezone code and CI runs that project separately.
- Absolute dates, a citation on every claim, grep before you record an absence.
- Postgres runs on `:5432` with the seeded `calendso` database; check `pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432`.

**Why this exists.** A host who is away from 14:00 to 16:00 today must block the whole day,
because out-of-office takes dates only. The product change is to block the hours the host is
away and keep the rest of the day bookable. The course reason: Sprint 1 D4 needs two medium
issues merged per member before the deadline, and #9 (PR #78) is the only other one.

**What is fixed.** Verified 2026-10-07 against `origin/main` at `fbae79557b`. Do not relitigate.
- Issue #6 already has the D2 spec: User Story, User Scenario, six acceptance criteria, Out of
  Scope, three Open Questions and Technical Notes. Labels `enhancement`, `effort:medium`; no
  `🚨 needs approval`; milestone Sprint 1; assignee `zach-short`. It has **no comments**, so the
  D2 teammate confirmation is still missing. Build to the six criteria as written.
- **No schema change is needed.** `OutOfOfficeEntry.start` and `end` are `DateTime`
  (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, model `OutOfOfficeEntry`, with `@@index([start, end])`).
- The tRPC input is `dateRange: { startDate, endDate }` plus `startDateOffset` and
  `endDateOffset` in minutes (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/ooo/outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.schema.ts`).
  The handler rounds to whole days at `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts:33-34`
  (`.startOf("day")`, `.endOf("day")`). Its overlap check (`:110-151`) already compares instants.
- **Stored values look like floating wall-clock times in UTC fields.** The handler adds the
  client's UTC offset, then truncates in UTC (`:33`); it reads back with `.tz(tz, true)` (`:348`);
  the slot code does the same at `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts:219`. Prove this
  with a test before you build on it: it decides how a time of day is stored.
- The form is `apps/web/modules/settings/outOfOffice/CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx` (436
  lines). Defaults at `:158-163` (today to today + 2 days); offsets sent at `:232-233`;
  `DateRangePicker` at `:251`; holiday suggestions read the range at `:182-188`.
- **Availability treats out-of-office as whole days.** `calculateOutOfOfficeRanges`
  (`packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts:727`) builds a map keyed
  `YYYY-MM-DD`; `buildDateRanges` turns each key into a full-day exclusion (`date-ranges.ts:263`,
  `oooExcludedDateRanges` at `:320`). The same map drives the booker's "away" and redirect display
  (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx`,
  `packages/features/calendars/weeklyview/components/DefaultOutOfOfficeSlot.tsx`). So criterion 4
  needs a slot-engine change. This is the heart of the item and the part that can fail silently.
- API v2 also forces whole days: `apps/api/v2/src/modules/ooo/inputs/ooo.input.ts:28-56` sets
  00:00:00.000 and 23:59:59.999 UTC. That stays as is.
- Tests to extend: `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.test.ts`,
  `packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.test.ts`, `packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.test.ts`.
- The PR needs: `Closes #6`; tests and a test strategy; a `## Design` section (D3: Decision,
  Alternatives considered (two or more), Rationale, Consequences); a teammate review with the
  Sprint 1 rubric; merge before the deadline. The AI-log reference goes in an **issue** comment,
  never in the PR. Keep it under 500 lines and 10 code files (`AGENTS.md`).
- PR #78 failed `Security Audit` and `required` in CI. The cause is not checked. Do not call a
  red check yours or not yours without running it on the base commit (`AGENT-PRACTICES.md` Part 6).

Do these, in order:
1. **Check before reading code:** your model; that #6 still has no `🚨 needs approval`; that no
   open PR touches the files in this row (`gh pr list --state open`, then `gh pr view <n> --json files`).
   PR #61 already turned out to be a duplicate of a board item; do not repeat that.
2. **Ask the questions below in one batch** and wait. The availability design decides the files.
3. **Make the worktree** with the fresh-checkout recipe (`yarn`, copy `.env`, `yarn prisma generate`)
   and record the baseline gate counts before your first edit.
4. **Form (criteria 1, 2, 5).** Add leave and return times beside the date range. Use a time input
   that already exists in this repo (grep `packages/ui` and the availability editor); do not
   invent one. New defaults: today to today, next full hour to three hours later. An end not after
   the start shows an error and does not save.
5. **Handler (criteria 3, 6).** Stop the day rounding when times are given. Keep existing entries
   unchanged: opening an old entry and saving without edits must not move its start or end. Test both.
6. **Slots (criterion 4).** Build the design Zach picks. Test with a host timezone that is not UTC
   (for example `America/New_York`), on a day that crosses a DST change, and at the window's exact
   edges: a slot that ends at the leave time is offered, one that overlaps it is not.
7. **Walk it in the browser** against `yarn dev`, logged in as seed user `pro`: create a 14:00 to
   16:00 entry today, then check the booking page offers slots before 14:00 and after 16:00 and none
   between. Delete the entry afterwards. Kill any dev server you started.
8. **Draft the PR body** at `docs/agent/sprint1-pr-draft-issue-6.md`, like
   `docs/agent/sprint1-pr-draft-issue-9.md`, with the `## Design` section.
9. **Record it:** a new `HANDOFF.md` step at the next free number, and this board row.

**Ask before building.** All of these are Zach's calls, and any answer may be no.
- **How the slot engine blocks a partial day.** (A) A partial-day entry becomes a busy time, like
  a calendar event, and stays out of the day map, so the booker shows no "away" or redirect for
  that day. Whole-day entries keep today's path. Smaller and lower risk. (B) The day map learns
  time ranges, so partial days also get the away and redirect display. Wider, touches the booker.
  This answer is also the D3 design decision for the PR.
- **How an entry counts as whole-day.** For example: start at 00:00 and end at 23:59:59.999 in the
  stored form, which every existing entry has. Or an "All day" toggle in the form, which adds UI copy.
- **The issue's three open questions:** near midnight, does the default end roll to the next day
  or stop at 23:59; do the times show in the out-of-office list; does redirect apply to a partial day.
- **Copy** (R7): two or three variants, with their register named, for the two time labels and the
  "end must be after start" error.
- **The cut if time runs short.** With the deadline on 2026-10-08, say early what fits. Criterion 4
  is the point of the issue, so shipping the form without it is a scope change only Zach can make.

**Not in scope, whoever asks:** API v2 and its DTOs; any schema change or migration; recurring
entries; the redirect, notes and reason fields; holiday suggestions beyond keeping them working;
issue #5; any file of PR #61 or PR #78.

**Hand back:** the files changed; gate counts against the baseline for
`yarn type-check:ci --force`, `yarn lint --force`, `TZ=UTC yarn test --exclude '**/.claude/**'`
and the timezone project; the browser walk stated separately from the gates; what Zach should
click to see it; the draft PR body path; and the two git blocks, which Zach runs.

## Gates

Measured 2026-09-14 in the primary checkout on **Node 22.14.0** (Node 26 breaks the toolchain —
see Known gaps). `HANDOFF.md` §Environment holds the setup recipe these depend on.

| Gate | Command | Where it comes from | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prisma types | `yarn prisma generate` | `unit-tests.yml:19`; `agents/rules/ci-type-check-first.md` | **exit 0** (exit 1 on Node 26) |
| Types | `yarn type-check:ci --force` | `package.json`; `check-types.yml:25`; `--force` per `AGENTS.md` | **exit 0** — 9 tasks, 0 cached, ~1m16–1m53 |
| Lint / format | `yarn lint --force` | `CONTRIBUTING.md` §Linting; `lint.yml:18` | **exit 0** — 11 tasks, 0 cached, 3970 files, **6091 warnings / 13144 infos / 0 errors** |
| Unit tests | `cal test` (= `TZ=UTC yarn test --exclude '**/.claude/**'`) | `package.json`; `unit-tests.yml:20` | **exit 0** — 407 files, 4119 tests (4069 passed, 47 skipped, 3 todo). Was 406 files before a database existed; test counts unchanged |
| Unit, timezone project | `VITEST_MODE=timezone yarn test --exclude '**/.claude/**'` | `unit-tests.yml:22`; `vitest.workspace.ts:7` | **exit 0** — 4 files, 64 tests (62 passed, 2 skipped) |
| Production build | `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1 yarn build` | `CONTRIBUTING.md` §Building | **exit 0** — 13 tasks, 0 cached, 2m46s. Bare `yarn build` exits 1 in 20s here, and *migrates the DB* where there is one (hazard 10) |

**Gates that can lie here.** The first five were verified by reading `.github/workflows/pr.yml`
on 2026-09-14; the last four were found by running the gates.

1. **A Markdown- or docs-only change runs no checks at all, and `required` passes.** `pr.yml`
   `prepare` computes `has-files-requiring-all-checks` with a paths-filter excluding
   `**/*.md`, `**/*.mdx`, `docs/**`, `help/**`, `.vscode/**`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `i18n.lock`
   and `packages/i18n/locales/**/common.json`. Green there means **nothing ran**.
2. **Without the `ready-for-e2e` label, every heavy job is skipped** — `build`, `build-api-v2`,
   `build-atoms`, `setup-db`, `integration-test` and all five e2e jobs are gated on
   `run-e2e == 'true'`. A green PR without that label ran lint, type-check, unit tests, api-v2
   unit tests and security-audit, and nothing else.
   `agents/rules/ci-check-failures.md` confirms this is expected, not a defect.
3. **A PR from anyone without write access runs zero checks until a maintainer adds `run-ci`**
   (`pr.yml` `trust-check`), and `required` then fails deliberately. That red is not yours.
4. **`check-prisma-migrations` only runs when `schema.prisma` or `migrations/**` changed.**
   Schema drift in any other PR is invisible.
5. **`turbo run type-check:ci` is cached.** A green run can be a replayed result. `--force`
   exists for exactly this and is not optional (`AGENTS.md`).
6. **`yarn lint` is cached too — and the documented command has no `--force`.** A run on
   2026-09-14 printed `Tasks: 11 successful ... Cached: 11 cached, 11 total >>> FULL TURBO`,
   having executed nothing. Because `AGENTS.md` prescribes `--force` for type-check and says
   nothing about lint, lint is the easier of the two to fool. Use `yarn lint --force`.
7. **A nested worktree doubles the test suite and turns it red.** Claude Code places worktrees
   at `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`, *inside* the repo root. Git ignores that path
   (`.git/info/exclude`); vitest does not. Measured 2026-09-14 on one unchanged tree:

   | | worktree present | `--exclude '**/.claude/**'` |
   |---|---|---|
   | exit | **1** | **0** |
   | files | 830 (208 failed) | 406 (0 failed) |
   | tests | 6323 (38 failed) | 4119 (0 failed) |

   All 208 "failures" were duplicates of real files, 202 of them `(0 test)` import errors
   because the nested checkout has source but no `node_modules`. `vitest list` exits 1 too.
   `type-check` and `lint` are unaffected — turbo scopes them to `package.json` `workspaces`
   (`apps/*`, `packages/*`, ...), which cannot match `.claude/worktrees/**`. **Run
   `git worktree list` before trusting a test count**, and note the baseline above was taken
   with the exclude flag, so a bare `TZ=UTC yarn test` will legitimately report more while a
   worktree exists. `--exclude` is additive in vitest 4.1.8 ("Additional file globs", verified
   via `yarn vitest --help`), so it does not disturb the config's own `node_modules` exclusion.

10. **`yarn build` applies database migrations, and fails confusingly without a database.**
   `packages/prisma`'s build script is `ts-node --transpile-only ./auto-migrations.ts`, which
   runs **`yarn prisma migrate deploy`** (`auto-migrations.ts:34`) against `DATABASE_URL`. So
   the command `CONTRIBUTING.md` tells you to run before pushing **mutates whatever database
   your `.env` points at** — never a shared or staging one. Its guard for a missing database is
   broken: `is-prisma-available-check.ts` returns `false` only for
   `Prisma.PrismaClientInitializationError` and rethrows everything else, so a refused
   connection escapes it and the build exits 1 at `@calcom/prisma#build` with
   ``Invalid `prisma.$queryRaw()` invocation`` — which reads as a code failure and is not one.
   `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1` (`auto-migrations.ts:17`) skips the step. Verified 2026-09-14.

8. **`yarn test` alone does not run the timezone project.** CI runs the suite twice — plain,
   then `VITEST_MODE=timezone` (`unit-tests.yml:20,22`), selected at `vitest.workspace.ts:7`.
9. **`yarn test` without `yarn prisma generate` fails on missing enums/types**, which reads as
   a code failure and is not one (`agents/rules/ci-type-check-first.md`). On Node 26 the
   generate step itself fails, so this compounds.

# Part 1 — The rules that hold everywhere

Each ends with its **test**, so whether a session complied is never a matter of opinion.
**"The owner"** is Zach.

**R1 — Absolute dates only.** `2026-09-14`, never "today", "recently", "last week".
*Test:* `grep -niE 'today|yesterday|recently|last (week|month)|this (week|month)'` over what
you wrote returns nothing.

**R2 — Every claim carries a citation.** `file:line`, a filename, a commit hash, a migration
name, the query that produced it. A claim with no citation is a guess and will be treated as
one.
*Test:* every sentence stating what the code, the data or the tooling does names its source;
one that cannot is deleted before hand-off.

**R3 — A claim in an existing doc is a lead, not a fact.** Re-verify before building on it.
This applies hardest to `AGENTS.md`, `agents/rules/**` and `students.md`: they are upstream
Cal.com's, describe a fast-moving codebase, and are not maintained against this fork.
*Test:* a claim carried forward appears with `verified <date>` and the citation from your own
check, not the original's.

**R4 — Grep before recording an absence.** "Nothing does X" is the most expensive kind of
wrong claim, because everything downstream is built on it. In a monorepo this size
(`apps/`, `packages/` — 595 Prisma migrations alone) the odds that a thing exists somewhere
are much higher than they feel.
*Test:* every "nothing does X" and "there is no X" carries the grep or query that produced it.

> **Worked example — another repo.** A handoff recorded "there is no vision anywhere in the
> repo". Vision was live the whole time in a helper file. On that track, "missing feature"
> claims were three for three wrong.

**R5 — When you disprove something, record the disproof where the wrong claim lives.** With
the reason it was wrong. Silent deletion means the next session rediscovers it. Where the
wrong claim is in a tracked upstream file you are not editing (R13), record the disproof in
`HANDOFF.md` under **Known API facts and quirks**, naming the file and line it corrects.
*Test:* the wrong claim is still findable, marked wrong, dated, with the disproof beside it.

**R6 — Ask the owner where he will see it, before building, in one batch.** That is the chat,
in the same turn. Questions written into a doc for async review do not get answered.
*Test:* the questions went out in one message before any code that depends on an answer was
written; the hand-back lists any still unanswered.

**R7 — For user-facing copy, never pick silently.** Write 2–3 real variations in different
registers (plain, warm, terse) and ask which. All UI strings also go in
`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` via `t()` (`AGENTS.md`;
`agents/rules/quality-review-checklist.md`), so the copy decision and the translation key
land together.
*Test:* the ask shows the variants with their registers named, or cites where the copy was
settled.

**R8 — Never re-litigate a settled decision.** Check for the settled/ratified marker before
treating anything as open — in `HANDOFF.md` under **Settled**, or in a spec's `decisions.md`
(`SPEC-WORKFLOW.md`). Genuinely new evidence produces a *supersession* — stated explicitly,
dated, naming what it replaces — not a quiet reversal.
*Test:* nothing carrying a settled marker is reopened; any change to one is a dated
supersession that names what it replaces.

**R9 — Descoping is the owner's call.** If something is explicitly parked, record it and stop
raising it. If nothing has been said, a finding still blocks by default: surface the judgment
call rather than making it.
*Test:* every finding not fixed appears in the hand-back as `parked by owner <date>` or
`open`; none is dropped silently.

**R10 — Report faithfully.** "Type-check green, not seen running" and "walked the booking flow
in the browser against seed data" are different claims and must never be merged. The PR
template's "How should this be tested?" section and `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s "Mention What Was
Tested (and How)" are the repo asking for exactly this; give it the true answer.
*Test:* the hand-back says which of the two it claims, per item.

**R11 — Read the matching standard in full before writing code.** Here that means `AGENTS.md`
plus the `agents/rules/*.md` files matching what you are touching — and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
Not optional, not conditional on task size. If you have not read them this session, read them
now.
*Test:* the session's first reads include them, and the hand-back names them.

**R12 — Stop mid-file when something contradicts a settled decision.** Do not take the call
and flag it afterwards. A build-level call that merely *implements* a settled decision is
yours to take — record it as a line in the `HANDOFF.md` step, with one line on how to reverse
it.
*Test:* the contradiction reaches the owner as a question before the next edit to that file
lands.

**R13 — The repo's own conventions outrank this file.** In this repo, in order:

> **1. `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `agents/rules/**`, `SPEC-WORKFLOW.md`, `biome.json`,
> the PR and issue templates.**
> **2. This standard, where they are silent.**
> **3. Nothing else.** Personal habit is not a standard, and neither is another repo's.

Where 1 and 2 disagree, **1 wins, 2 is wrong, and 2 gets amended.** Cite their rule rather
than restating it (8.5) — `agents/rules/data-prefer-select-over-include.md`, not a paraphrase
of it. The same rule at file scale: **match the file you are in.** A diff that is visually
distinguishable from the code around it is a defect even when every line is defensible alone.
*Test:* the posture table above holds, and a reader of the diff cannot pick out the new lines
by style alone.

**R14 — A gate goes green by fixing the finding.** Never loosen a check to pass: not a Biome
rule, not a type, not an assertion, not a threshold, not a CI config. `as any` is already
banned outright (`AGENTS.md`), and a widened type, a `.skip`, a deleted assertion or a blanket
ignore is the same move wearing different clothes. **Green means the recorded baseline or
better** — which, until Known gap 1 is closed, means you must first *establish* the baseline
rather than assert one. A genuine exception is narrow, carries its reason inline
(`@ts-expect-error -- reason`), and is named in the hand-back. If a failure is genuinely not
yours, **prove it** the way Part 6 describes, and say so.
*Test:* the diff contains no new suppression, skip, deleted assertion or relaxed config
without a reason inline and a line in the hand-back; the findings count did not rise and the
test count did not fall.

**R15 — Never use an API you have not seen exist.** Options, config keys, flags, methods, CLI
arguments: verify against the version installed *in this checkout* — `node_modules`, `yarn.lock`,
the package's own types — and cite what you read. This repo pins `yarn@4.12.0`, Biome schema
`2.3.10` (`biome.json:2`) and a large pinned dependency set; a plausible invented option is the
single most common way agent-written code reaches a reviewer broken. Prisma is the sharpest
case: run `yarn prisma generate` and read the generated types rather than assuming a field
or enum exists.
*Test:* every API introduced either already appears elsewhere in the repo or carries a
citation to where its existence was verified.

**R16 — Secrets never enter the repo, the docs, or a pasted transcript.** No credentials, no
`.env` contents, no tokens, no connection strings — not in code, not in a fixture, not in a
doc, not in a pass-off prompt, not in a log you paste. `.env` is gitignored
(`.gitignore:4,41`) and `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` / `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are generated locally
(`students.md`); neither ever appears in a file that is written down. Where one must appear in
a record, **redact it in place and mark the redaction** (`[redacted: API key]`) rather than
deleting the turn. If one has already landed: say so immediately and rotate it.
*Test:* the diff and every block in the hand-back are read for credentials before either is
posted; every redaction is marked; any leak is named in the hand-back the same session.

# Part 6 — Parallel sessions

The assumption throughout: **several sessions run against this repo at once, and the owner is
the only one who knows which uncommitted file belongs to whom.** Worktrees live under
`.claude/worktrees/`, which is already excluded (`.git/info/exclude`) — so a worktree never
shows up as untracked noise in the primary checkout.

## Identity and guardrails, once per machine

- **The commit identity must be one GitHub recognises.** If `user.email` is not an address
  attached to the account, commits land unattributed — no contribution history, and no fix
  short of rewriting history. For a course repo where attribution *is* part of the
  deliverable, verify it on GitHub rather than trusting the config.

```bash
git config user.name "<name>" && git config user.email "<an address GitHub knows>" && git config --get user.email
```

- **Confirm the guardrails are real before you need them.** Push a throwaway branch, confirm
  it succeeds, and confirm you **cannot** push to `main`. A rejected push there is a correct
  result, better learned now than at a hand-back.

## The fresh-checkout recipe — worktree or clone

A fresh checkout fails gates for purely environmental reasons before it fails a real one. All
of this runs on entry, **before believing any gate**:

# 0. yarn must exist. Verified 2026-09-14: neither `yarn` nor `corepack` is on PATH on this
#    machine (node is v26.7.0 at /opt/homebrew/bin/node). One of:
#       npm i -g corepack && corepack enable        # then yarn resolves from packageManager
#       npm i -g yarn@4.12.0                        # packageManager pins yarn@4.12.0
yarn --version                 # must print 4.12.0 (package.json "packageManager")

# 1. Dependencies IN THIS CHECKOUT. `git worktree add` copies none of them.
yarn

# 2. Gitignored-but-required env. `.gitignore:4,41` hides these; nothing creates them.
cp .env.example .env
#    then set NEXTAUTH_SECRET  (openssl rand -base64 32)
#         and CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY (openssl rand -base64 24)   — students.md
#    Never paste either value into a doc, a prompt or a transcript (R16).

# 3. Generated Prisma client + types. `.gitignore:69-74` hides them; missing enum/type errors
#    are this, not your code (agents/rules/ci-type-check-first.md).
yarn prisma generate

# 4. Prove it, do not assert it. Paste the output, not the word "done".
yarn type-check:ci --force
```

The three classes that bite, and all three are live here:

- **Gitignored-but-required files** — `.env` and the generated Prisma client. Without them,
  gates fail naming code you never touched.
- **Dependencies not installed in the checkout** — until they are, an intra-repo
  `@calcom/*` workspace package may resolve elsewhere, so a green typecheck proves nothing
  about your edits.
- **Caches shared across checkouts** — `.turbo` is per-checkout, but `turbo run type-check:ci`
  will happily replay a cached result. `--force` is the answer and is not optional.

  > **Worked example — another repo.** A red lint gate reporting 20 findings came back *clean*
  > when re-run with an isolated cache — the findings belonged to a sibling worktree. Re-run
  > with a fresh cache before believing a red.

**Always go through the repo's own scripts** (`yarn type-check:ci`, `yarn lint`, `yarn test`),
never a bare `tsc`, `biome` or `vitest`. The scripts route through `turbo` with the repo's
filters and configs; a bare invocation selects a different configuration and fails in ways
that have nothing to do with your change.

## Before you debug a red gate, find out whose it is

**Check whether it is red without your change**, before forming a single theory. Not by
stashing — the stash stack is shared with every other worktree and another session may pop
yours — but in a throwaway checkout of the base commit:

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/base $(git merge-base HEAD main) && cd /tmp/base && yarn && yarn prisma generate && yarn type-check:ci --force
```

A failure that reproduces there is a note in the hand-back and an item on the board, not an
afternoon. **This is also how R14's "prove it is not yours" is satisfied**: state the command,
where you ran it, and its output.

## Committing under a shared index

These bind whoever commits — which per Part 11 is the owner, running the blocks this session
prints. They are stated here because the blocks must be *correct* when printed.

```bash
git add -N <new-path> && git commit -o <path> <path> -m "..."
```

- **`git add -N` first for any file git has never seen.** `--only` silently drops untracked
  paths, and the commit still typechecks, because the files are on disk.
- **Never `git add -A`, never `git add .`**, not even scoped to a directory. It sweeps up
  another session's in-flight work — and it is the one command that would drag this
  standard's own files toward a commit. Git refuses an explicitly named excluded path; that
  refusal is the net working and is **never** answered with `-f`.
- **Commit early, in small slices** — after each leg lands, not once at the end. This is also
  the repo's own rule (`CONTRIBUTING.md`: <500 lines, <10 code files).

  > **Worked example — another repo.** A whole feature build was swept into a parallel
  > session's commit while its author was still running gates.

- **Never `git checkout --` or bare `git stash`/`git stash pop` to undo an experiment.** Both
  reach files that are not yours, and the stash stack is shared across every worktree of this
  clone. Copy the file aside and restore it with `cp`, or make a throwaway WIP commit.
- **After a split commit, build HEAD in isolation before pushing.** Gates run against the
  working tree, not HEAD, so a partial commit can leave the branch unbuildable while your tree
  is green:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/headcheck && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/headcheck && cd /tmp/headcheck && yarn && yarn prisma generate && yarn type-check:ci --force
```

- **Shell working directory resets between calls in some harnesses.** Use absolute paths for
  anything whose answer depends on which checkout you are in.

## Numbered shared resources — Prisma migrations

`packages/prisma/migrations/` holds **595 migrations plus `migration_lock.toml`** (verified
2026-09-14), named `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description`. They are timestamps, not a sequence, so two
sessions do not collide on a *number* — they collide on **order**, which is worse because it
is silent: a migration with an earlier timestamp created later will be applied out of the
order it was written against.

- **Derive the timestamp at the moment you create the migration**, from the clock, via
  `yarn prisma migrate dev --create-only --name <name>` (`agents/rules/data-prisma-feature-flags.md`).
  Never copy a timestamp from a doc, a plan or this file.
- **Read names, not counts.** `ls | wc -l` is not the latest migration.
- **Rebase onto `main` before pushing a migration**, and re-check that yours is still last.
- `check-prisma-migrations` only runs in CI when `schema.prisma` or `migrations/**` changed —
  so it will catch drift in your PR, and nowhere else.
- Schema changes are on `AGENTS.md`'s **Ask first** list. They are the owner's call.

## Other shared state

- **A dev server already listening on the port** will be reused, which then silently tests the
  previous build. Kill any hand-started one first.
- **A test database pointed at the wrong target** can skip every test and still print `ok`.
  Grep the output for skips rather than trusting the exit code, and check the count against
  the recorded baseline. `agents/rules/ci-check-failures.md` also names two CI-only errors to
  ignore outright ("password authentication failed for user postgres", "Invalid URL").
- **A warm client reading cache** can make a data fix look unfixed. If the server log shows no
  request, you are reading cache, not the system.

---

# Part 7 — Closing a piece of work

**Every item ends the same way, in this order, without being asked.** The point is that the
owner can close the session immediately after: set the stated model, paste the blocks, go.

### 1 — Read your own diff, top to bottom

Before the record, before the blocks. `git diff` and `git status --short`, every hunk, looking
for the things that pass gates and fail people:

- **a credential, token or `.env` line anywhere in it** (R16) — checked first, because it is
  the only item here that cannot be fixed after the fact;
- an API, option, Prisma field or enum you did not verify exists in this checkout (R15);
- `include` where `select` belongs, or any query that could return `credential.key`
  (`agents/rules/data-prefer-select-over-include.md`; `AGENTS.md`);
- `as any`, anywhere (`AGENTS.md`);
- a test that asserts the mock rather than the behaviour — green, worthless, and it will be
  trusted;
- anything loosened to go green: a widened type, a disabled rule, a `.skip`, a deleted
  assertion (R14);
- comments describing *what* the line does, and any protected comment deleted (Part 11;
  `agents/rules/quality-code-comments.md`);
- **files touched that the task never named** — the scope creep is the finding;
- a barrel import, or an import that does not match the file it lives in (R13).

Anything you cannot explain does not ship. Delete it or understand it.

### 2 — Update the record

- One new `HANDOFF.md` step at the next free number (read it; do not trust one written
  elsewhere), naming what changed, why, what is now fixed, and which questions it answered.
  Add new files to the code map. Do not edit a step you did not write.
- For a `specs/` effort, also update that spec's `implementation.md` and `decisions.md` **in
  the repo's own format** (`SPEC-WORKFLOW.md`) — those are tracked and go in the commit.
- **The `HANDOFF.md` record is updated in the same session and never appears in a commit.**
  The commit carries the code (and any `specs/` update) alone, its message in the repo's own
  style — conventional commits, `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` (`AGENTS.md`) — with no
  reference to a ledger step nobody else can read.
- **Landed early on budget, or interrupted?** Same ritual, different header: leave the item
  unmarked, add a status note — what is done, what is left, what it changes about the plan —
  and write the handoff. The pass-off then targets *the remainder of this item*. Also write a
  handoff when work crosses a model boundary. If the owner says stop, stop; mid-item is fine.

### 3 — Post three blocks in the hand-back

In the chat, not only in the docs: the whole value is that they are copy-pasteable at the
moment the session ends.

- **Block A — the pass-off prompt.** Part 3, in full, as a fenced block. It must stand alone.
- **Block B — the runtime entries this piece added.** The lines the owner walks, pasted here
  while the work is fresh.
- **Block C — the next session's model, on its own line.** `Next session: <tier>` — plus one
  clause on why, if it differs from the last. Last in the message, because it is the first
  thing the owner acts on.

Then the two commit blocks from Part 11, which the owner runs.

### 4 — State plainly what was and was not verified

R10. Give the gate counts against the recorded baseline rather than the word "green"; name any
exception taken under R14; name any pre-existing failure you are claiming is not yours, with
its evidence from Part 6; name any redaction made under R16. If a gate could not be run at
all — which, until Known gap 1 is closed, is the normal case — **say that, rather than
reporting the ones you could run as if they were the set.**

## Recording what actually shipped

**Every deviation from the plan is written back under the decision it deviates from** — not as
a changelog at the bottom, not in a commit message, but inline where someone reading that
decision will hit it. This is the anti-drift mechanism, and the single habit that separates
documentation you can trust from documentation you cannot.

Record equally: when the plan left a choice open and the build picked one; when the build found
the plan's premise wrong; and when a scope item was dropped. Refresh the live numbers too — the
gate baselines if they legitimately moved, the latest migration name, any dial that got a real
value.

## The runtime pass

**Each piece of work writes its own runtime entries as it goes**, and pastes them into the
hand-back at close (Block B). Not reconstructed later. An entry is three lines:

- **Goal it is checking** — what behaviour should now be true, in product terms.
- **Where** — the exact screen or endpoint, and how to reach it (which is also what
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks the PR description for).
- **What the right answer is** — including the fixture. If the check needs specific data, give
  the query or the seeded user that finds it (`yarn db-seed` creates `free:free` and `pro:pro`
  — `agents/rules/reference-local-dev.md`), not an id that will rot.

The owner walks the pass. **It does not block the work or the close-out.** What it blocks is
*claiming* something was seen working when it was not. Findings fold back as a new item, not
as ad-hoc fixes.

## Archiving a `specs/` effort

`SPEC-WORKFLOW.md` does not define an archive step, and inventing one for a tracked directory
would be setting policy in someone else's repo (R13). So: **leave a closed `specs/<slug>/`
where it is**, mark its `implementation.md` status as complete in the repo's own words, and
record the closure — plus anything the spec leaves behind that still governs the code — in
`HANDOFF.md` under **Invariants** or **Known API facts**. A rule nobody can find is a rule
nobody follows.

`docs/agent/archive/` exists for the *private* layer only: a superseded ledger, an old board.
Before moving anything there, grep for referrers — `git ls-files | xargs grep -l <filename>` —
and verify each file actually arrived before trusting the deletion.

**This standard applies forward from 2026-09-14.** Work done before then is a historical
record, not a conversion target. Do not retrofit.

# Contributing to Cal.diy

> **Important:** Cal.diy is a community-driven, open-source fork of Cal.com. Contributions made here **do not** get merged into Cal.com's production service — Cal.com is now closed-source. This repo is maintained independently by the community under the MIT license.

Contributions are what make the open source community such an amazing place to learn, inspire, and create. Any contributions you make are **greatly appreciated**.

## House Rules (for PRs and Issues)

### 👥 Prevent Work Duplication

Before submitting a new issue or PR, check if it already exists in the [Issues](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/issues) or [Pull Requests](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/pulls).

### ✅ Work Only on Approved Issues

For feature requests, please wait for a core team member to approve and remove the `🚨 needs approval` label before you start coding or submitting a PR.

For bugs, security, performance, documentation, etc., you can start coding immediately—even if the `🚨 needs approval` label is present.

We highly value new feature ideas, but to maintain consistency in the product direction, they must go through a review and approval process.

### 🚫 Don’t Just Drop a Link

Avoid posting third-party links (e.g., Slack threads or Linear tickets) without context. A GitHub issue or PR should stand on its own—reviewers shouldn’t have to chase information across multiple tools to understand the context.

### 👀 Think Like a Reviewer

Put yourself in the reviewer’s shoes. What would you want to know if reading this for the first time? Are there key decisions, goals, or constraints that need clarification? Does the PR assume knowledge that isn’t obvious? Are there related issues or previous PRs that should be linked?

### 🧵 Bring in Context from Private Channels

If the task originated from a private conversation (e.g., Slack), take a moment to extract the relevant details and include them in the GitHub issue or PR. Avoid sharing sensitive information, but make sure important reasoning is captured.

> Example:  
> “A user requested feature X to solve problem Y. I considered approaches A, B, and C, but chose C for the following reasons…”

### 📚 Treat It Like Documentation

GitHub is a shared source of truth. Every issue and PR contributes to the long-term understanding of the codebase. Write clearly enough that someone—possibly you—can revisit it months later and still understand what happened and why.

### ✅ Summarize Your PR at the Top

Even if the code changes are minor or self-explanatory, a short written summary helps reviewers quickly understand the intent. You can use GitHub Copilot’s auto-summarize feature, but make sure to verify it for accuracy and relevance.

### 🔗 Use GitHub Keywords to Auto-Link Issues

Use phrases like “Closes #123” or “Fixes #456” in your PR descriptions. This automatically links your PR to the related issue and closes it once merged—keeping everything traceable and organized.

### 🧪 Mention What Was Tested (and How)

Explain how you validated your changes. It doesn’t need to be exhaustive—just enough to give reviewers confidence that things were tested and work as expected.

> Example:  
> “Tested locally with mock data and confirmed the flow works on staging.”

### 🧠 Assume Future-You Won’t Remember

Write with the future in mind. If there are trade-offs, edge cases, or temporary workarounds, document them clearly so they don’t get lost or misinterpreted later.

## File Naming Conventions

To ensure consistency and make files easy to fuzzy-find, we follow the naming conventions below for **services**, **repositories**, and other class-based files.

### Repository Files

- Repository class files must include the `Repository` suffix.
- If the repository is backed by a specific technology (e.g. Prisma), prefix the filename and class name with it.
- File name must match the exported class exactly (PascalCase).

**Pattern:**

`Prisma<Entity>Repository.ts`

**Examples:**

```ts
// File: PrismaAppRepository.ts
export class PrismaAppRepository { ... }

// File: PrismaMembershipRepository.ts
export class PrismaMembershipRepository { ... }
```

This avoids ambiguous filenames like app.ts and improves discoverability in editors.

### Service Files

- Service class files must include the Service suffix.
- File name should be in PascalCase, matching the exported class.
- Keep naming specific — avoid generic names like AppService.ts.

**Pattern:**

`<Entity>Service.ts`

**Examples:**

```ts
// File: MembershipService.ts
export class MembershipService { ... }

// File: HashedLinkService.ts
export class HashedLinkService { ... }
```

**Note:**

- New files must avoid dot-suffixes like .service.ts or .repository.ts; these will be migrated from the existing codebase progressively.
- We still reserve suffixes such as .test.ts, .spec.ts, and .types.ts for their respective use cases.

## Developing

[See README](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy#development)

## Building

You can build the project with:

```bash
yarn build
```

Please ensure that you can make a full production build before pushing code.

## Testing

More info on how to add new tests coming soon.

### Running Tests

[See README](https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy#e2e-testing)

#### Resolving Issues

Run `npx playwright install` to download test browsers and resolve the error below when running `yarn test-e2e`:

Executable doesn't exist at /Users/alice/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-1048/chrome-mac/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium
```

## Linting

To check the formatting of your code:

```sh
yarn lint
```

If you get errors, be sure to fix them before committing.

## Making a Pull Request

### Keep PRs Small and Focused

Large PRs are difficult to review and more prone to errors. We strongly encourage smaller, self-contained PRs:

- **Size limits**: Keep PRs under 500 lines of code changed and under 10 code files modified (excludes documentation, lock files, and auto-generated files)
- **Single responsibility**: Each PR should address one concern (one feature, one bug fix, or one refactor)
- **Split large changes**: If your task requires extensive changes, break it into multiple PRs that can be reviewed and merged independently

**How to split large changes:**
- Separate database/schema changes from application logic
- Split frontend and backend changes when possible
- Do preparatory refactoring in a separate PR before adding new features
- Create PRs in dependency order (infrastructure first, then features)

### PR Checklist

- Be sure to [check the "Allow edits from maintainers" option](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork) when creating your PR. (This option isn't available if you're [contributing from a fork belonging to an organization](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/5634))
- If your PR refers to or fixes an issue, add `refs #XXX` or `fixes #XXX` to the PR description. Replace `XXX` with the respective issue number. See more about [linking a pull request to an issue](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue).
- Fill out the PR template accordingly.
- Review the [App Contribution Guidelines](./packages/app-store/CONTRIBUTING.md) when building integrations.
- Lastly, make sure to keep your branches updated (e.g., click the `Update branch` button on the GitHub PR page).

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what the problem is.
  For example, "I'm always frustrated when..."
-->

As a user, I want to be able to schedule times that I am out of office down to the minutes. Currently, I am only able to schedule out of office in day-sized chunks of time. I want to be able to say that I am out of office for only a few hours.

### Describe the solution you'd like

<!--
  Provide a clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->
In addition to having days in the OOO scheduling page, having a leave time and return time. Make the default dates set to the same day (ie Sep 12, 2026-Sep 12, 2026) with the time out of the office being nearest next hour through nearest next hour plus three hours (ie. if it is 16:30, make the automatically selected OOO times 17:00-20:00).


### User Story

As a user, I want to set out-of-office periods with a leave time and a return time, so that I block only the hours I am away and not the whole day.

### User Scenario

A host has an appointment from 14:00 to 16:00. Today the out-of-office form takes dates only and the server stretches the entry to the whole day, so the host must block all of it. After this change, the host opens the out-of-office form, keeps today as the date, sets leave 14:00 and return 16:00, and saves. Attendees can still book at 09:00 and 17:00 that day, but no slot is offered between 14:00 and 16:00.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The create and edit out-of-office form has a leave time and a return time in addition to the date range.
2. When the form opens to create a new entry, both dates default to today, the leave time defaults to the next full hour, and the return time defaults to three hours after the leave time. At 16:30 the defaults are 17:00 and 20:00.
3. After saving, the stored start and end match the chosen dates and times in the host's timezone, not the start of the first day and the end of the last day.
4. Booking slots inside the out-of-office window are not offered. Slots on the same day outside the window are still offered.
5. If the end date and time is not after the start date and time, the form shows an error and does not save.
6. Entries created before this change keep blocking the same period. Opening one for edit and saving without changes does not alter its start or end.

### Out of Scope

- Recurring out-of-office entries.
- Changes to the redirect, notes or reason fields.
- Changes to the holiday suggestions in the form, beyond keeping them working.

### Open Questions

- Near midnight the defaults cross a date boundary (at 22:30 the next full hour is 23:00 and three hours later is 02:00 the next day). Should the end date roll to the next day, or should the end be capped at 23:59?
- Should the leave and return times also show in the out-of-office list?
- Does an entry that starts and ends on a time inside one day need any change in how the redirect (forward to another user) applies?

### Technical Notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)

- `OutOfOfficeEntry.start` and `end` are already `DateTime` columns (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, model `OutOfOfficeEntry`), so a schema change may not be needed. The planning doc assumed one.
- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/ooo/outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts` rounds the start to the start of the day and the end to the end of the day. This is the part that must change.
- `apps/web/modules/settings/outOfOffice/CreateOrEditOutOfOfficeModal.tsx` currently defaults to today through two days later, so criterion 2 changes the default.

## What does this PR do?

- Fixes #9

Leaving the event type editor with unsaved edits used to throw them away without a word. Now a
click on any link that leaves the editor (the sidebar, the top navigation, or the back arrow in the
header) opens a dialog first. "Save" saves and then goes where the user clicked.
`Don't save and leave` goes there without saving. Escape or the close button keeps the user on the
page with the edits intact. With no edits, or right after a save, links work as before and no dialog appears.

"Has unsaved edits" is the same signal that enables the header Save button,
`formMethods.formState.isDirty` (`EventTypeLayout.tsx:279`). Issue #10 (#20) made that signal
trustworthy on load, so the dialog and the Save button always agree.

**How it works.** The App Router has no API for blocking a navigation, and the editor's existing
`useHandleRouteChange` hook only runs after the pathname has already changed. So the new
`useUnsavedChangesGuard` hook listens for link clicks on `document` in the capture phase while the
form is dirty. That listener runs before `next/link`'s own handler, which returns early when the
event is already `defaultPrevented` (`next/dist/client/app-dir/link.js:319` in Next 16.2.3). The
hook stops the click and remembers the destination; the dialog then decides what happens. It lets
a click through when the link opens a new tab (Cmd, Ctrl, Shift or middle click, or
`target="_blank"`), when it points to another site, and when it stays on the same page. The last
case covers the editor's own tabs, which only change `?tabName=` and keep the form state.

"Save" in the dialog runs the same submit path as the header Save button. It resolves to `true`
only when the update mutation succeeds. If the server rejects the save, the existing error toast
appears and the user stays on the page. If the form is invalid, the user also stays and sees
"Error updating settings".

**Two changes outside the editor, both small.**

1. `Shell.tsx`: when `backPath` is a string, the header back arrow is now a real link
   (`<Button href>`) instead of a button that calls `router.push`. A click listener cannot see
   where a button is going, so without this the editor could not guard its own back arrow. The
   destination is unchanged on every page that uses `backPath`. The visible difference is that
   the arrow can now be middle-clicked into a new tab. `backPath={true}` still calls
   `router.back()`.
2. Closing or reloading the tab with unsaved edits now shows the browser's own "Leave site?"
   prompt (`beforeunload`). The browser fixes its wording, and it cannot offer Save.

**Decided with the issue owner (2026-10-07).** The issue's open question, whether the browser Back
button should open the dialog, is answered **no**. Next 16 reloads the page on Back for any
history entry that lacks its private `__NA` state (`next/dist/client/components/app-router.js:284`),
so guarding Back means writing that private state ourselves. That is fragile across Next upgrades,
and it belongs in its own issue if anyone wants it.

**Known limits.** Browser Back is not guarded, as above. Navigation started from code rather than
from a link, such as the Cmd+K menu, is not guarded either, because it never passes through a link
click. Links to other sites fall to the browser's own prompt.

**Files.** New: `apps/web/modules/event-types/hooks/useUnsavedChangesGuard.ts` (+ test),
`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/dialogs/UnsavedChangesDialog.tsx` (+ test). Changed:
`EventTypeWebWrapper.tsx` (wiring), `Shell.tsx` (back arrow), `en/common.json` (3 strings). 493
lines of code, 301 of them tests.

  calculateOutOfOfficeRanges(
    outOfOfficeDays: GetUserAvailabilityInitialData["outOfOfficeDays"],
    availability: GetUserAvailabilityParamsDTO["availability"]

    if (!outOfOfficeDays || outOfOfficeDays.length === 0) {
      return {};
    }

    return outOfOfficeDays.reduce(
      (acc: IOutOfOfficeData, { start, end, toUser, user, reason, notes, showNotePublicly }) => {
        // here we should use startDate or today if start is before today
        // consider timezone in start and end date range
        const startDateRange = dayjs(start).utc().isBefore(dayjs().startOf("day").utc())
          ? dayjs().utc().startOf("day")
          : dayjs(start).utc().startOf("day");

        // get number of day in the week and see if it's on the availability
        const flattenDays = Array.from(
          new Set(availability.flatMap((a) => ("days" in a ? a.days : [])))
        ).sort((a, b) => a - b);

        const endDateRange = dayjs(end).utc().endOf("day");

        for (let date = startDateRange; date.isBefore(endDateRange); date = date.add(1, "day")) {
          const dayNumberOnWeek = date.day();

          if (!flattenDays?.includes(dayNumberOnWeek)) {
            continue; // Skip to the next iteration if day not found in flattenDays
          }

            showNotePublicly,
          };
        }

        return acc;
      },

    );

    // but not using these values at all, wasting CPU. Adding this check here temporarily to avoid a larger refactor
    // since other callers do using this data.
    if (returnDateOverrides) {
      const calculateDateOverridesSpan = Sentry.startInactiveSpan({ name: "calculateDateOverrides" });
      const availabilityWithDates = availability.filter((availability) => !!availability.date);

      for (let i = 0; i < availabilityWithDates.length; i++) {
        const override = availabilityWithDates[i];
        const startTime = dayjs.utc(override.startTime);
        const endTime = dayjs.utc(override.endTime);
        const overrideStartDate = dayjs.utc(override.date).hour(startTime.hour()).minute(startTime.minute());
        const overrideEndDate = dayjs.utc(override.date).hour(endTime.hour()).minute(endTime.minute());
        if (
          overrideStartDate.isBetween(dateFrom, dateTo, null, "[]") ||
          overrideEndDate.isBetween(dateFrom, dateTo, null, "[]")
        ) {
          dateOverrides.push({
            start: overrideStartDate.toDate(),
            end: overrideEndDate.toDate(),
          });
        }
      }

      calculateDateOverridesSpan.end();
    }

    const outOfOfficeDays =
      initialData?.outOfOfficeDays ??
      (await this.dependencies.oooRepo.findUserOOODays({
        userId: user.id,
        dateFrom: dateFrom.toISOString(),
        dateTo: dateTo.toISOString(),
      }));

    const datesOutOfOffice: IOutOfOfficeData = this.calculateOutOfOfficeRanges(outOfOfficeDays, availability);

    const holidayBlockedDates = await this.calculateHolidayBlockedDates(
      user.id,
      dateFrom.toDate(),
      dateTo.toDate(),
      availability
    );

    for (const [date, holidayData] of Object.entries(holidayBlockedDates)) {
      if (!datesOutOfOffice[date]) {
        datesOutOfOffice[date] = holidayData;
      }
    }

    const travelSchedules: {
      startDate: Dayjs;
      endDate?: Dayjs;
      timeZone: string;
    }[] = [];

    if (isDefaultSchedule) {
      travelSchedules.push(
        ...user.travelSchedules.map((schedule) => {
          let endDate: Dayjs | undefined;
          if (schedule.endDate) {
            endDate = dayjs(schedule.endDate);
          }
          return {
            startDate: dayjs(schedule.startDate),
            endDate,
            timeZone: schedule.timeZone,
          };
        })
      );
    }

    const { dateRanges, oooExcludedDateRanges } = buildDateRanges({
      dateFrom,
      dateTo,
      availability,
      timeZone: finalTimezone,
      travelSchedules,
      outOfOffice: datesOutOfOffice,
    });

    if (dateRanges.length === 0)
      return {
        busy: [],
        timeZone: finalTimezone,
        dateRanges: [],
        oooExcludedDateRanges: [],
        workingHours: [],
        dateOverrides: [],
        currentSeats: [],
        datesOutOfOffice: undefined,
      };

    const { bookingLimits, durationLimits } = await this.parseLimits(eventType);

    // TODO: only query what we need after applying limits (shrink date range)
    const getBusyTimesStart = dateFrom.toISOString();
    const getBusyTimesEnd = dateTo.toISOString();

    const selectedCalendars = eventType?.useEventLevelSelectedCalendars
      ? user.allSelectedCalendars.filter((calendar) => calendar.eventTypeId === eventType.id)
      : user.userLevelSelectedCalendars;

    let busyTimesFromLimits: EventBusyDetails[] = [];
    if (initialData?.busyTimesFromLimits && initialData?.eventTypeForLimits) {
      busyTimesFromLimits = initialData.busyTimesFromLimits.get(user.id) || [];
    } else if (eventType && (bookingLimits || durationLimits)) {
      busyTimesFromLimits = await getBusyTimesFromLimits(
        bookingLimits,
        durationLimits,
        dateFrom.tz(finalTimezone),
        dateTo.tz(finalTimezone),
        duration,
        eventType,
        initialData?.busyTimesFromLimitsBookings ?? [],
        finalTimezone,
        initialData?.rescheduleUid ?? undefined
      );
    }

    const teamForBookingLimits =
      initialData?.teamForBookingLimits ??
      eventType?.team ??
      (eventType?.parent?.team?.includeManagedEventsInLimits ? eventType?.parent?.team : null);

    const teamBookingLimits = parseBookingLimit(teamForBookingLimits?.bookingLimits);

    let busyTimesFromTeamLimits: EventBusyDetails[] = [];

    if (initialData?.teamBookingLimits && teamForBookingLimits) {
      busyTimesFromTeamLimits = initialData.teamBookingLimits.get(user.id) || [];
    } else if (teamForBookingLimits && teamBookingLimits) {
      // Fall back to individual query if not available in initialData
      busyTimesFromTeamLimits = await getBusyTimesFromTeamLimits(
        user,
        teamBookingLimits,
        dateFrom.tz(finalTimezone),
        dateTo.tz(finalTimezone),
        teamForBookingLimits.id,
        teamForBookingLimits.includeManagedEventsInLimits,
        finalTimezone,
        initialData?.rescheduleUid ?? undefined
      );
    }

    let busyTimes = [];
    try {
      const busyTimesService = getBusyTimesService();
      busyTimes = await busyTimesService.getBusyTimes({
        credentials: user.credentials,
        startTime: getBusyTimesStart,
        endTime: getBusyTimesEnd,
        eventTypeId,
        userId: user.id,
        userEmail: user.email,
        username: `${user.username}`,
        beforeEventBuffer,
        afterEventBuffer,
        selectedCalendars,
        seatedEvent: !!eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot,
        rescheduleUid: initialData?.rescheduleUid || null,
        duration,
        currentBookings: initialData?.currentBookings,
        bypassBusyCalendarTimes,
        silentlyHandleCalendarFailures,
        mode,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      log.error(`Error fetching busy times for user ${username}:`, error);
      return {
        busy: [],
        timeZone: finalTimezone,
        dateRanges: [],
        oooExcludedDateRanges: [],
        workingHours: [],
        dateOverrides: [],
        currentSeats: [],
        datesOutOfOffice: undefined,
      };
    }

    const detailedBusyTimesWithSource: EventBusyDetails[] = [
      ...busyTimes.map((a) => ({
        ...a,
        start: dayjs(a.start).toISOString(),
        end: dayjs(a.end).toISOString(),
        title: a.title,
        source: a.source,
      })),
      ...busyTimesFromLimits,
      ...busyTimesFromTeamLimits,
    ];

    const detailedBusyTimes: UserAvailabilityBusyDetails[] = withSource
      ? detailedBusyTimesWithSource
      : detailedBusyTimesWithSource.map(({ source, ...rest }) => rest);

    log.debug(
      `EventType: ${eventTypeId} | User: ${username} (ID: ${userId}) - usingSchedule: ${safeStringify({
        chosenSchedule: schedule,
        eventTypeSchedule: eventType?.schedule,
      })}`
    );

    const formattedBusyTimes = detailedBusyTimes.map((busy) => ({
      start: dayjs(busy.start),
      end: dayjs(busy.end),
    }));

    const dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailable = subtract(dateRanges, formattedBusyTimes);
    const dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailableWithoutOOO = subtract(oooExcludedDateRanges, formattedBusyTimes);

    const result = {
      busy: detailedBusyTimes,
      timeZone: finalTimezone,
      dateRanges: dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailable,
      oooExcludedDateRanges: dateRangesInWhichUserIsAvailableWithoutOOO,
      workingHours,
      dateOverrides,
      currentSeats,
      datesOutOfOffice,
    };

    log.debug(
      `EventType: ${eventTypeId} | User: ${username} (ID: ${userId}) - Result: ${safeStringify(result)}`
    );

    return result;
  }

  /**
   * This fn mainly uses _getUserAvailability but sends busy times from limits too to _getUserAvailability as expected by _getUserAvailability.

export type DateRange = {
  start: Dayjs;

export type WorkingHours = Pick<Availability, "days" | "startTime" | "endTime">;

type TravelSchedule = { startDate: Dayjs; endDate?: Dayjs; timeZone: string };

function getAdjustedTimezone(date: Dayjs, timeZone: string, travelSchedules: TravelSchedule[]) {
  let adjustedTimezone = timeZone;

  for (const travelSchedule of travelSchedules) {
    if (
      !date.isBefore(travelSchedule.startDate) &&
      (!travelSchedule.endDate || !date.isAfter(travelSchedule.endDate))
    ) {
      adjustedTimezone = travelSchedule.timeZone;
      break;
    }
  }
  return adjustedTimezone;
}

  it("should mark slots as away when OOO is on next day and availability extends past midnight", async () => {
    // This test reproduces the bug where:
    // - Day 1 has availability from 00:00 to 23:59
    // - Day 2 is marked as OOO
    // - Slots generated after midnight are not marked as away

    vi.setSystemTime(dayjs.utc("2025-11-17T00:00:00Z").toDate());

    const day1Start = dayjs.utc("2025-11-17T00:00:00Z");
    const day2End = dayjs.utc("2025-11-18T23:59:59Z");

    // OOO data for Day 2 (2025-11-18)
    const datesOutOfOffice = {
      "2025-11-18": {
        fromUser: { id: 1, displayName: "Test User" },
        toUser: null,
        reason: "Out of office",
        emoji: "🏖️",
      },
    };

    const slots = getSlots({
      inviteeDate: day1Start,
      frequency: 15,
      minimumBookingNotice: 0,
      eventLength: 15,
      dateRanges: [
        {
          start: day1Start,
          end: day2End,
        },
      ],
      datesOutOfOffice,
      datesOutOfOfficeTimeZone: "UTC",
    });

    const day1Slots = slots.filter((slot) => slot.time.format("YYYY-MM-DD") === "2025-11-17");
    const day2Slots = slots.filter((slot) => slot.time.format("YYYY-MM-DD") === "2025-11-18");

    // Day 1 slots should NOT be marked as away
    day1Slots.forEach((slot) => {
      expect(slot.away).toBeUndefined();
    });

    expect(day2Slots.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);

    // Day 2 slots should be marked as away
    day2Slots.forEach((slot) => {
      expect(slot.away).toBe(true);
      expect(slot.reason).toBe("Out of office");
      expect(slot.emoji).toBe("🏖️");
    });

    vi.useRealTimers();
  });

```text
    log.debug(
      `EventType: ${eventTypeId} | User: ${username} (ID: ${userId}) - Called with: ${safeStringify({
        params,
      })}`
    );

    const user = initialData?.user || null;
    if (!user) {
      throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 404, message: "No user found in getUserAvailability" });
    }

    let eventType: EventType | null = initialData?.eventType || null;
    if (!eventType && eventTypeId) eventType = await this.getEventType(eventTypeId);
    /* Current logic is if a booking is in a time slot mark it as busy, but seats can have more than one attendee so grab
    current bookings with a seats event type and display them on the calendar, even if they are full */
    let currentSeats: CurrentSeats | null = initialData?.currentSeats || null;
    if (!currentSeats && eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot) {
      currentSeats = await this.getCurrentSeats(eventType, dateFrom, dateTo);
    }

    const { isDefaultSchedule, isTimezoneSet, schedule } = detectEventTypeScheduleForUser({
      eventType,
      user,
    });

    if (
      !(
        schedule?.availability ||
        (eventType?.availability.length ? eventType.availability : user.availability)
      )
    ) {
      throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: ErrorCode.AvailabilityNotFoundInSchedule });
    }

    const availability = (
      schedule?.availability || (eventType?.availability.length ? eventType.availability : user.availability)
    ).map((a) => ({
      ...a,
      userId: user.id,
    }));

    let calendarTimezone: string | null = null;
    let finalTimezone: string | null = null;

    if (!isTimezoneSet) {
      calendarTimezone = await this.getTimezoneFromDelegatedCalendars(user);
      if (calendarTimezone) {
        finalTimezone = calendarTimezone;
      }
    }

    if (!finalTimezone) {
      finalTimezone = schedule.timeZone;
    }

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Add the whole-day predicate and partial-day range builder to the date-ranges module

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("packages/features/schedules/lib/date-ranges.ts")
s = p.read_text()
old = """// This function processes out-of-office dates and returns a date range for each OOO date.
function processOOO(outOfOffice: Dayjs, timeZone: string) {
  const OOOdate = outOfOffice.tz(timeZone, true);
  return {
    start: OOOdate,
    end: OOOdate,
  };
}
"""
new = """// This function processes out-of-office dates and returns a date range for each OOO date.
function processOOO(outOfOffice: Dayjs, timeZone: string) {
  const OOOdate = outOfOffice.tz(timeZone, true);
  return {
    start: OOOdate,
    end: OOOdate,
  };
}

// The create handler strips the client's UTC offset before saving, so OutOfOfficeEntry.start and .end hold
// the host's wall-clock time in UTC columns. An entry saved as whole days spans 00:00:00.000 to 23:59:59.999.
export function isWholeDayOutOfOffice({ start, end }: { start: Date; end: Date }): boolean {
  return (
    start.getUTCHours() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCMinutes() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCSeconds() === 0 &&
    start.getUTCMilliseconds() === 0 &&
    end.getUTCHours() === 23 &&
    end.getUTCMinutes() === 59 &&
    end.getUTCSeconds() === 59 &&
    end.getUTCMilliseconds() === 999
  );
}

// `.tz(timeZone, true)` (keepLocalTime, which processOOO uses for midnight) resolves a wall-clock time that
// falls within a few hours of a DST change against the wrong offset: 03:30 on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York
// came back as 04:30-05:00. Parsing the wall-clock string in the zone returns 03:30-04:00.
function wallClockToTimeZone(stored: Date, timeZone: string): Dayjs {
  return dayjs.tz(dayjs.utc(stored).format("YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSS"), timeZone);
}

export function getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges(
  entries: { start: Date; end: Date }[],
  timeZone: string
): DateRange[] {
  return entries
    .filter((entry) => !isWholeDayOutOfOffice(entry))
    .map(({ start, end }) => ({
      start: wallClockToTimeZone(start, timeZone),
      end: wallClockToTimeZone(end, timeZone),
    }));
}
"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))
print("date-ranges.ts updated")
PY

Add optional start and end times to the input schema and apply them in the handler

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/ooo/outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.schema.ts")
s = p.read_text()
old = """import { z } from "zod";

export const ZOutOfOfficeInputSchema = z.object({
  uuid: z.string().nullish(),
  forUserId: z.number().nullish(),

new = """import { z } from "zod";

const ZTimeOfDay = z.string().regex(/^([01]\\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\\d$/);

export const ZOutOfOfficeInputSchema = z.object({
  uuid: z.string().nullish(),
  forUserId: z.number().nullish(),
  dateRange: z.object({
    startDate: z.date(),
    endDate: z.date(),
  }),
  startDateOffset: z.number(),
  endDateOffset: z.number(),
  // "HH:mm" on the start and end dates. Absent means the whole day, which is what every client sent before.
  startTime: ZTimeOfDay.optional(),
  endTime: ZTimeOfDay.optional(),
  toTeamUserId: z.number().nullable(),
"""
assert s.count(old) == 1
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))

h = pathlib.Path("packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/ooo/outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts")
s = h.read_text()
old_imp = 'import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";\n'
new_imp = 'import type { Dayjs } from "@calcom/dayjs";\nimport dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";\n'
assert s.count(old_imp) == 1
s = s.replace(old_imp, new_imp)
old_body = """export const outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate = async ({ ctx, input }: TBookingRedirect) => {
  const { startDate, endDate } = input.dateRange;
  if (!startDate || !endDate) {
    throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "start_date_and_end_date_required" });
  }

  const startTimeUtc = dayjs.utc(startDate).add(input.startDateOffset, "minute").startOf("day");
  const endTimeUtc = dayjs.utc(endDate).add(input.endDateOffset, "minute").endOf("day");

  // If start date is after end date throw error
  if (startTimeUtc.isAfter(endTimeUtc)) {
    throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "start_date_must_be_before_end_date" });
  }
"""
new_body = """const atTimeOfDay = (day: Dayjs, time: string) => {
  const [hours, minutes] = time.split(":").map(Number);
  return day.hour(hours).minute(minutes);
};

export const outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate = async ({ ctx, input }: TBookingRedirect) => {
  const { startDate, endDate } = input.dateRange;
  if (!startDate || !endDate) {
    throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "start_date_and_end_date_required" });
  }

  // Adding the client's offset turns the instant into the host's wall-clock time, which is then kept in the
  // UTC columns. A time of day is applied to that wall-clock date. An end of 23:59 means the end of the day,
  // as it does for date overrides, so a 00:00-23:59 entry is stored like a whole-day entry.
  const startDayUtc = dayjs.utc(startDate).add(input.startDateOffset, "minute").startOf("day");
  const endDayUtc = dayjs.utc(endDate).add(input.endDateOffset, "minute").startOf("day");
  const startTimeUtc = input.startTime ? atTimeOfDay(startDayUtc, input.startTime) : startDayUtc;
  const endTimeUtc =
    input.endTime && input.endTime !== "23:59" ? atTimeOfDay(endDayUtc, input.endTime) : endDayUtc.endOf("day");

  if (!startTimeUtc.isBefore(endTimeUtc)) {
    throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "start_date_must_be_before_end_date" });
  }
"""
assert s.count(old_body) == 1
h.write_text(s.replace(old_body, new_body))
print("schema + handler updated")
PY

  it("offers the slot that ends at the leave time and none that overlaps the window", async () => {
    const result = await service.getUserAvailability(params, {
      user,
      outOfOfficeDays: [outOfOfficeEntry("2026-10-08T14:00:00.000Z", "2026-10-08T16:00:00.000Z")],
    });

    const slots = getSlots({
      inviteeDate: dayjs.tz("2026-10-08T00:00:00", timeZone),
      frequency: 60,
      eventLength: 60,
      minimumBookingNotice: 0,
      offsetStart: 0,
      dateRanges: result.dateRanges.filter(
        (range) => range.start.tz(timeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD") === "2026-10-08"
      ),
    });

    // 09:00 to 13:00 EDT start a one-hour slot that ends by 14:00; 16:00 EDT is the first slot after the return.
    expect(slots.map((slot) => slot.time.toISOString())).toEqual([
      "2026-10-08T13:00:00.000Z",
      "2026-10-08T14:00:00.000Z",
      "2026-10-08T15:00:00.000Z",
      "2026-10-08T16:00:00.000Z",
      "2026-10-08T17:00:00.000Z",
      "2026-10-08T20:00:00.000Z",
    ]);
  });

  it("keeps a whole-day entry on the away map and out of the OOO-excluded ranges", async () => {
    const result = await service.getUserAvailability(params, {
      user,
      outOfOfficeDays: [outOfOfficeEntry("2026-10-08T00:00:00.000Z", "2026-10-08T23:59:59.999Z")],
    });

    expect(result.datesOutOfOffice).toEqual({
      "2026-10-08": {
        fromUser: { id: 1, displayName: "Host" },
        toUser: null,
        reason: null,
        emoji: null,
        notes: null,
        showNotePublicly: false,
      },
    });
    expect(rangesOn(result.dateRanges, "2026-10-08")).toEqual([
      ["2026-10-08T13:00:00.000Z", "2026-10-08T21:00:00.000Z"],
    ]);
    expect(rangesOn(result.oooExcludedDateRanges, "2026-10-08")).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("blocks a window that runs past midnight across both days", async () => {
    const result = await service.getUserAvailability(params, {
      user,
      outOfOfficeDays: [outOfOfficeEntry("2026-10-07T16:00:00.000Z", "2026-10-08T10:00:00.000Z")],
    });

    expect(rangesOn(result.dateRanges, "2026-10-07")).toEqual([
      ["2026-10-07T13:00:00.000Z", "2026-10-07T20:00:00.000Z"],
    ]);
    expect(rangesOn(result.dateRanges, "2026-10-08")).toEqual([
      ["2026-10-08T14:00:00.000Z", "2026-10-08T21:00:00.000Z"],
    ]);
    expect(result.datesOutOfOffice).toEqual({});
  });
});

  options.push({ value: dayEnd.format("HH:mm"), label: dayEnd.format(labelFormat) });

+// The create handler strips the client's UTC offset before saving, so OutOfOfficeEntry.start and .end hold
+// the host's wall-clock time in UTC columns. An entry saved as whole days spans 00:00:00.000 to 23:59:59.999.
+export function isWholeDayOutOfOffice({ start, end }: { start: Date; end: Date }): boolean {
+  return (
+    start.getUTCHours() === 0 &&
+    start.getUTCMinutes() === 0 &&
+    start.getUTCSeconds() === 0 &&
+    start.getUTCMilliseconds() === 0 &&
+    end.getUTCHours() === 23 &&
+    end.getUTCMinutes() === 59 &&
+    end.getUTCSeconds() === 59 &&
+    end.getUTCMilliseconds() === 999
+  );
+}
+
+// `.tz(timeZone, true)` (keepLocalTime, which processOOO uses for midnight) resolves a wall-clock time that
+// falls within a few hours of a DST change against the wrong offset: 03:30 on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York
+// came back as 04:30-05:00. Parsing the wall-clock string in the zone returns 03:30-04:00.
+function wallClockToTimeZone(stored: Date, timeZone: string): Dayjs {
+  return dayjs.tz(dayjs.utc(stored).format("YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSS"), timeZone);
+}
+
+export function getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges(
+  entries: { start: Date; end: Date }[],
+  timeZone: string
+): DateRange[] {
+  return entries
+    .filter((entry) => !isWholeDayOutOfOffice(entry))
+    .map(({ start, end }) => ({
+      start: wallClockToTimeZone(start, timeZone),
+      end: wallClockToTimeZone(end, timeZone),
+    }));
+}

+const buildTimeOptions = (timeFormat: number | null | undefined): TimeOption[] => {
+  const labelFormat = timeFormat === 12 ? "h:mma" : "HH:mm";
+  const dayStart = dayjs.utc("1970-01-01T00:00:00Z");

+  for (let minutes = 0; minutes < 24 * 60; minutes += TIME_OPTION_STEP_MINUTES) {

+// Stored values are the host's wall-clock time in UTC columns, so they are formatted in UTC.
+const formatOutOfOfficePeriod = ({ start, end }: { start: Date; end: Date }) => {
+  const startDay = dayjs.utc(start);
+  const endDay = dayjs.utc(end);
+  if (isWholeDayOutOfOffice({ start, end })) {
+    return `${startDay.format("ll")} - ${endDay.format("ll")}`;
+  }
+  if (startDay.isSame(endDay, "day")) {
+    return `${startDay.format("ll LT")} - ${endDay.format("LT")}`;
+  }
+  return `${startDay.format("ll LT")} - ${endDay.format("ll LT")}`;
+};

# PR draft: issue #6 (out-of-office with a leave time and a return time)

**Status: NOT OPENED.** Built 2026-10-08 in worktree `.claude/worktrees/issue-6`, branch
`feat/issue-6-ooo-leave-return-time` off `origin/main` at `792b42d067`. Open it as a **draft PR**
(`agents/rules/quality-pr-creation.md`) after the commit and push.

- **Title:** `feat: set a leave time and a return time for out of office (#6)`
- **Base:** `main`
- **Media to drag in:** <<MEDIA>>

Everything below the line is the PR body.
